title: KPMG audit partner quits after pressure from Westpac
full_text:
KPMG audit partner Kim Lawry will leave the consulting giant and its board immediately, after being pushed out from the $32m-a-year Westpac audit account.
Westpac met with KPMG this week and called for Ms Lawry to be taken off its audit team as the lender sought to put some distance between it and the scandal engulfing the accounting firm.
KPMG engagement partner Brendan Twining will step in as the lead partner on the Westpac account A KPMG spokesman said Ms Lawry, a veteran audit partner, was retiring in the wake of Westpac seeking her removal from its account. “Kim Lawry is stepping down from the KPMG Australia board effective today and retiring from the partnership after a smooth transition of her responsibilities,” he said.
In her resignation letter, Ms Lawry referenced the “strong team culture and personal connections” she had built with KPMG as well as her positive relationships with clients.
“It is the trust my clients have placed in me that gives me a great sense of pride – supporting them through some of their most important and challenging moments is a responsibility I have never taken for granted,” Ms Lawry wrote.
In a separate letter to the Westpac audit team, Ms Lawry praised its work on the account.
“I have always been very open and honest in my role leading this team and the Westpac audit. With that in mind, I wanted you to all hear directly from me that I have made the decision to retire from the KPMG Australia partnership,” Ms Lawry wrote. “Whilst I appreciate that this is unsettling news, I remain committed to ensuring that we are focused on delivering the best for Westpac.
“We have a great leadership team and, myself along with all the partners, are committed to ensuring a smooth transition and that FY26 is every bit as big a success as FY25 – and even more so.” A Westpac spokesman said the bank had requested Ms Lawry remove herself from its audit account.
“To ensure there is no distraction from the delivery of Westpac’s FY26 audit, Westpac, in consultation with KPMG, asked lead audit partner Kim Lawry to step aside from the Westpac audit engagement,” the spokesman said. “We thank Kim for her commitment and contribution to ensuring a smooth transition over the past two years and welcome Brendan (Twining) to the role.” Ms Lawry’s exit comes as the audit giant faces a public reckoning over allegations its senior audit staff misused confidential client documents from Lendlease and Dexus to pitch for work at other firms, including Westpac.
The scandal has now claimed the scalps of KPMG’s leadership, including chairman Martin Sheppard, CEO Andrew Yates, head of audit Julian McPherson and chief operating officer Eileen Hoggett.
KPMG last month fined Ms Lawry and two others for accessing confidential Lendlease board papers as it was pitching for Westpac’s audit account. Ms Hoggett and partner Paul Rogers resigned last month.
Ms Lawry exits KPMG and the Westpac account weeks after Westpac director Peter Nash stepped down from the bank’s board amid the audit scandal. Mr Nash worked at KPMG for 25 years and chaired the firm from 2011 to 2017 before he joined the Westpac board in 2018. His exit came almost a month after The Australian revealed he had slept over at the house of Mr Sheppard as the audit firm pitched for the Westpac audit – worth $32m a year.
